articles.title: Watermark Capital Moves Forward With School-to-Resi Conversion in Crown Heights
articles.narrative: Watermark Capital Group is moving forward with the conversion of a former Roman Catholic school campus in Crown Heights, Brooklyn, into a 42-unit residential building and a community facility. The developer secured a $16.48 million construction loan from Genesis Capital for the project, which involves a vertical expansion of an existing building. Watermark Capital Group previously obtained a ground lease for the site from St. Teresa of Avila Roman Catholic Church.

data_points.notable_features: The project includes a 42,181-square-foot residence and a 57,449-square-foot community facility.
data_points.project_notes: The site was previously a school campus owned by St. Teresa of Avila Roman Catholic Church. Watermark Capital Group obtained a ground lease for the site in April 2024, which was modified in June 2025.

articles.title: Jay Roberts of Prosper Group: 5 Questions
articles.narrative: Developer Jay Roberts, CEO of Prosper Group, recently acquired a 1-acre waterfront site along the Miami River in Miami's Brickell district for $50 million. The site, which includes 66 Southwest Sixth Street and 625 Southwest First Avenue, is slated for a two-phase luxury high-rise development, with the first phase planned as a 60-story residential tower with 181 units. Roberts, who transitioned from Wall Street, emphasizes his firm's focus on best-in-class waterfront development sites and leveraging his finance background for capital raising and joint venture structuring.

data_points.notable_features: Waterfront site with 300 feet of river frontage, located near Brickell City Centre.
data_points.project_notes: The acquisition is for a two-phase project, with the first phase being a 60-story luxury residential high-rise.

articles.title: Ten Legal Due Diligence Priorities for Hotel Investors
articles.narrative: This article outlines key legal due diligence priorities for investors in hotel acquisitions, emphasizing that hotel deals often fail due to a lack of understanding of the business implications of property and operational issues, rather than obscure legal technicalities. The author, drawing on decades of experience, highlights the importance of thoroughly examining franchise agreements, management contracts, environmental conditions, and entitlements. Investors are advised to scrutinize assumable financing and ground leases, understand the labor landscape, and verify what assets and liabilities are truly being acquired beyond just the real estate. The piece underscores that hotels are operating businesses, not just real estate assets, requiring a comprehensive legal review that goes beyond standard property due diligence.

articles.title: A big impact: Interstate Capital planning five industrial developments along Michigan’s Interstate-94 corridor

Consumer Prices Rise 0.4% in August as Gasoline Costs Accelerate
articles.narrative: U.S. consumer prices increased by 0.4% in August, driven primarily by a significant rise in gasoline and other energy costs. The Consumer Price Index (CPI) saw a 3.4% annual increase through August, consistent with July's pace. While core CPI, excluding food and energy, rose 0.3% for the month and 2.4% annually, the acceleration in energy prices was the main factor contributing to the overall headline inflation pressure. Shelter costs, a substantial component of the CPI, also saw a 0.3% increase for the month.

articles.title: Report: Tariffs Won’t Impact Every U.S. Market in the Same Way
articles.narrative: A recent report by Cushman & Wakefield analyzes the uneven impact of U.S.-Canada tariffs across different U.S. markets, noting that states like Maryland, Kentucky, Texas, and Michigan have above-average exposure due to their reliance on heavily tariffed imports such as automotive parts and aluminum. Despite this, the report indicates that trade accounts for a relatively small portion of these states' GDP. The analysis suggests several implications for commercial real estate, including increased demand for third-party logistics and bonded warehouses as companies adopt 'just-in-case' inventory strategies and seek to delay tariff payments. Additionally, tariffs could accelerate onshoring trends, particularly in the automotive sector, and lead to higher development costs due to material-cost inflation, potentially shifting developer focus towards higher-conviction projects.

articles.title: Logos Faith Tests Modular Construction for Affordable Housing Scale
articles.narrative: Logos Faith Development is exploring modular construction as a method to accelerate its affordable housing pipeline, which currently includes over 2,000 units across 30 faith-based partnerships. The non-profit is testing this approach at the Logos-Grant Housing Apartments in South Los Angeles, a project being developed in partnership with Model/Z. The goal is to evaluate if modular construction can deliver more units faster and at a lower cost, potentially accounting for half of Logos Faith's future developments, while still utilizing traditional construction methods for other projects.

data_points.address: 105th Street and Central Avenue, Los Angeles, CA
data_points.notable_features: Project is a test case for modular construction methods.
data_points.project_notes: The project is in the permitting stage, with Ready to Issue (RTI) permits completed in nine months, significantly faster than the typical 18 months.
